title: Serve a pancake from a frying pan with a spatula
description: Use a pre-held flexible kitchen turner with a dexterous hand (Sharpa Wave by default, or Wuji Hand 2.2) to slide its blade under a cooked pancake in a frying pan, carry it on the blade to a ceramic plate, deposit it flat in the plate and withdraw the turner; a dropped or hand-touched pancake or a knocked pan or plate fails the episode at once.
mechanism: free rigid pancake carried by a hand-held turner with passive bending strips
instruction: Serve the pancake from the frying pan onto the plate using the kitchen turner (spatula) that the hand already holds. The pancake lies in the frying pan, the empty ceramic plate stands beside it on the counter, and the turner starts in a power grasp of the hand. Only the turner may move the pancake: slide its blade under the pancake, lift it out of the pan on the blade, carry it to the plate, set it down in the plate and withdraw the turner. Success requires three stages in this order. (1) On the blade: the pancake touches the turner blade and no other object (no pan, plate, hand, counter or floor contact), its origin is at least 0.015 m above its starting height and it is tilted at most 30 degrees, for 10 consecutive controls. (2) Over the plate: later, while still touching only the turner, the pancake centre is within 0.058 m (horizontally) of the plate centre and above the plate floor. (3) Served: later, the pancake touches only the plate, its centre is within 0.058 m of the plate centre horizontally (the whole pancake inside the plate's 0.128 m rim radius), it is tilted at most 20 degrees from flat, its linear speed is at most 0.02 m/s and angular speed at most 0.3 rad/s, the turner does not touch it and every point of the blade outline is at least 0.08 m from the pancake centre horizontally (withdrawn); this complete condition must hold for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success at that moment; skipping or reordering a stage never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 1 ms physics substep with no grace period, when the pancake touches the counter top or the floor, falls freely (touching nothing while its centre of mass moves down faster than 0.35 m/s, i.e. after about 6 mm of free fall) or its origin falls below the counter top (z < 0.85 m), when any part of the hand touches the pancake, when the turner touches the floor, falls out of the hand (no hand contact while its centre of mass moves down faster than 0.35 m/s) or its origin falls below the counter top, when the pan or the plate moves more than 0.03 m from its starting position or tilts more than 15 degrees, when the pancake, pan, plate or turner leaves the workspace box x in [0.23, 1.13] m, y in [-0.65, 0.45] m, z in [0.80, 1.50] m, or when the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed; no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct object forces. The pancake is a rigid coherent disk and the turner blade bends through three passive spring hinges. The episode allows at most 3000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.
modeling: Free rigid pan (0.90 kg), plate (0.48 kg), coherent pancake (0.06 kg, 140 mm x 9.5 mm) and turner (0.15 kg) from the T16 scene; the turner blade is three passive bending strips (EI/length from a 0.25 mm steel core). Concave pan/plate interiors use convex sector contacts. The turner starts in a settled power grasp (contact only, no weld). Pair frictions are declared estimates: pancake-pan 0.45, pancake-blade 0.20, blade-pan 0.20, pancake-plate 0.60, hand-handle 1.2, objects-counter 0.7. Rigid cooked food: no deformation, tearing, heat or fluid model.
